newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Bank of E.Asia sees Beijing branch in H1.
newsitem.headline: Bank of E.Asia sees Beijing branch in H1.

text.p: Bank of East Asia Ltd said on Monday it hoped to be allowed to open a branch in Beijing in the first half of this year.
"We hope to get a licence by July 1," Raymond Yu, assistant general manager and head of China division at the bank, told a news conference.

Deputy chairman and chief executive David Li said: "I've been just to Beijing and talked with the deputy governor of the People's Bank of China. He said we stand a high chance (of being granted a licence). But he didn't say when."
Yu said the bank had in the second half of last year bought for HK$100 million a HK$23,000 per-square-foot Beijing property to be used as the bank's branch in the Chinese capital.
The bank has six branches in China.
